title: Closure evidence: adopt the useful parts of the 10/10 closure proposal (decision record)
body:
## Closure evidence — what we take from the "10/10 closure superstructure" proposal

**Dylan Roy — delegated AI work.** Actual performer: Anthropic Claude, Claude Code session `017Mi3hx` (this lane is the author of the Math-#160, #167, #173 and #183 register records and of the D1 Theorem A review; that exposure matters for items 5 and 6 below). Scientific effect: **NONE**. Read at main `cddbb7f6` and Math- `08f8686c`. Dylan forwarded the proposal on 2026-10-06 and pre-approved whatever the team decides. This issue is the decision record. Each adopted item still lands as a normal PR with a nonauthor review and a separate integrator.

### Bottom line

1. **About half the proposal already exists here under other names.** The dependency graph with fail-closed promotion, non-discharge tokens (green CI, hashes, self-review never discharge), the mandatory witness-collision gate, loss-only demotion, certified outward arithmetic, a novelty/priority ledger, and exposure-aware review records are all in place.
2. **The biggest single step toward the proposal's goal is not new tooling.** It is executing the three reviewed, merged register records Math-#167, #160 and #173. They have been executable since the readiness repair (Math-#183 plus C110 Math-#250, 3 October). No lane has executed them. Until then GRAPH lags STATUS for D2/D3/D4/D5-annulus/D6, and the witness-collision node stays `OPEN_ACTIVE` even though a reviewed discharge exists.
3. **Two items are genuinely new and worth adopting.** These are blind reconstruction (a reviewer who never saw the proof) and a dedicated adversarial "attack" review. Every review we have is source-exposed; our own review form already calls that "the weakest form of review".
4. **We decline anything that creates a second status register or vocabulary.** That covers a `CLOSED` status word, a hand-maintained passport file and new top-level `/closure` directories. AGENTS.md says "do not introduce another vocabulary or scientific register", and the workflow says "Do not create another global ownership or scientific-status register". Closure is instead reported as a *derived* evidence profile computed from records we already keep.

### Item-by-item decision

| # | Proposal item | What we already have (exact location) | Decision | Next action / owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Proof passport per theorem | GRAPH node records carry source fingerprint, scope, reading rule, review source and author/reviewer providers (`Math-/frontiers/downstream_gate_20260925/GRAPH.json`). STATUS rows carry explicit limits. `claims/LANDING_CLAIMS.json` | **ADAPT** | A derived, read-only evidence profile and dependency tree generated from those records. It is never hand-edited and never committed as a status file. Axes with no record print `not recorded`. **Claude lane authors** (Math- PR) |
| 2 | New `CLOSED` status | The ladder already exists as separate predicates: `PROVED_REVIEWED` (graph terminal); formal `kernel-checked` plus alignment `accepted` (`formal/README.md`); organizational-independence credit; Dylan's personal reading `PENDING`; and the rule that AI work cannot fill an independent-human-review requirement | **DECLINE as a status word** | No register change. The profile in item 1 shows which predicates hold |
| 3 | Formalize only the load-bearing invariants | `formal/ResearchFormalCoreR1` (63 declarations, kernel-checked gate with axiom audit and negative controls). `frontiers/cap_first_exit_lean_20261002` (cap first-exit / elder-merge step with Hessian bounds). D2Schur and the companions | **ADAPT** | Tier A gap: the fold normal form itself (critical points, Hessian signs, critical-value gap of order r³) and the multiplicity-two / reciprocal identity are exact-checked in packets (`separated_fold_multiplicity_20261002`, C026), not formalized. This is a pickup slot for the existing formal lane under the existing gate. Tier B is already covered by certified outward-arithmetic packets (`coefficients/side24_*`, the C6 tail constants, the cusp coefficient). Tier C stays in the proof architecture |
| 4 | Independent AI reconstruction without the proof | None. All reviews so far are source-exposed | **ADOPT** | New review basis "Blind reconstruction". The packet holds statement, assumptions, definitions and allowed literature only. The reconstructor declares zero exposure; under shared accounts, only a fresh session with no repository access is credible. The reconstruction is published before a third party compares the dependency graphs. Pilot: D1 Theorem A (`0 <= 1-p_r <= C r^3`) |
| 5 | "Destroy the theorem" lane | Ad-hoc precedents: the PR #114 challenge found missed prior art; the P15 demand-one exact counterexample; the C7 refutation; the exact falsification probes | **ADOPT** | New review basis "Adversarial attack", with the proposal's checklist (missing hypotheses, non-uniform o(·), limit interchange, boundary terms, degeneracies, multiple witnesses, candidate/bar confusion, conditioning, hidden independence, exceptional configurations, scaling regimes, dimension). The output is `counterexample found` / `not found` plus remaining attack surfaces. First target: the witness-collision discharge (#160/#173), by a **non-Claude** lane, run in parallel with item 6 |
| 6 | Hardest open interface as a mandatory gate | `math.rn-region.witness-collision` is `OPEN_ACTIVE`; `hard_gate.promotion_allowed` refuses promotion while a required node is non-terminal; PROOF_INDEX states "NO COMPLETE REGIONAL PROOF YET" | **ALREADY HAVE** | **Execute** Math-#167, #160 and #173 in that order (non-Claude lane; the three checkers plus the readiness workflow are the gate, and nothing in the packets is regenerated). The dry run moves the register from 49 nodes / 55 edges to 88 / 131. The hard gate stays OK, no new hold appears and three holds clear. **Re-run today** (`execution_dryrun.py --out <scratch>` at Math- `08f8686c`): `passed: true`, 88 / 131, and nothing in the repository was written. GRAPH and SELECTOR_REGION are unchanged since 2026-09-29. If item 5 later finds a defect, loss-only reverse impact demotes the affected nodes |
| 7 | Theorem-level dependency compiler | `hard_gate.closure_report` (layers, hold proposals, `gate_ok`); `reverse_impact_between` (loss-only) | **HAVE (machine) + ADAPT (human view)** | (a) A readable tree in the item 1 tool. (b) The item 6 execution. (c) Then a declarative proposal for one headline node (the ℓ^(-1/3) / short-lifetime chain), so "conditional because exactly one dependency remains" can be read off. A proposal author writes it; a non-Claude lane executes it |
| 8 | Two structurally independent numerical implementations | Outward-rounded enclosures, two-mode replays and ad-hoc cross-checks (for example, the #297/#299 raw-moment check agreed to 5.5e-115) | **ADAPT** | Convention for headline constants only (c_{d,24}, C_U(1), tail constants): a second implementation by a different method and a nonauthor lane, recorded in that packet's review record (no new ledger). First target: c_{2,24} |
| 9 | Literature novelty gate | `main/docs/RECON_NOVELTY_20260925.md` and `DISCOVERY_PRIORITY_LEDGER_20260925.md`. Amended 09-27 after a nonauthor challenge found missed prior art; their rule is "to our knowledge …, never 'first'" | **HAVE, STALE** | Refresh for results since 09-27 (C6 Palm Θ(r³), C7, the C8 window coefficients d=2…7, the D2 Schur floors, LM006). Use two independent searches told to find "someone already proved this", and amend the existing ledger |
| 10–11 | Short human referee packet; adversarial human review | Delegated-review rule; personal reading `PENDING`; AI cannot fill independent human review; the planar manuscript `main/docs/research-translation/20260930/MANUSCRIPT.md` with `PERSISTENCE_BRIDGE.md` | **ADOPT the packet; the referee is Dylan's call** | A packet of 20 pages or fewer for D1: theorem, definitions, at most six critical lemmas, dependency DAG, assumption ledger, open interfaces, certificates, and the blind reconstruction when available. It asks one question: "identify the earliest unsupported inference". Any lane may build it. Choosing and contacting a human referee is an owner decision |
| 12 | New `/closure`, `/reproduction` directories | `reviews/`, `certificates/`, `coefficients/`, `formal/`, `frontiers/downstream_gate_20260925/` | **DECLINE** | Use the existing homes. No duplicate trees |
| 13 | Definition of 10/10; failure lowers status | Loss-only transitions (`reverse_impact_between` → HOLD/REVALIDATION) | **ADOPT as the profile axes** | These are descriptive axes only. A failed axis lowers the profile and never edits proof bytes |

### Order of work (highest value per effort first)

1. **Execute #167 → #160 → #173** (non-Claude lane). This is the largest unlock, and its gates already exist.
2. **Review-form + protocol PR in main** adding the blind-reconstruction and adversarial-attack bases. *Claude lane, authoring now.*
3. **Attack review of the witness-collision discharge** (non-Claude; this lane authored #160/#173).
4. **Derived evidence-profile / dependency-tree tool in Math-**, read-only and standard library. *Claude lane, authoring now.*
5. **Novelty-ledger refresh** using two independent searches.
6. **Tier A fold-normal-form Lean module** in the existing formal lane.
7. **Second implementation of c_{2,24}** by a lane that is not the author of side24.
8. **Blind reconstruction pilot on D1 Theorem A.** This needs an unexposed session; Dylan can start one in a fresh chat with no repository tools.
9. **D1 referee packet.** The human referee is Dylan's decision.

### What this decision does not do

It changes no STATUS, PROOF_INDEX, GRAPH, catalog or register row. It does not flip `lemma_closed`, prizes or premises, and adds no new status word, register, scheduler or timer. Items 1–13 are protocols and derived views. Scientific acceptance keeps its existing predicates.

**Objections:** if a lane objects to a row, post it here with a concrete reason before the affected PR is integrated. Otherwise these dispositions stand under Dylan's pre-approval. Claim a pickup slot with an ordinary `PICKUP` comment on this issue, naming the item number.
